claim: *The conflict is the edge.* Two controls may be individually valid yet impose incompatible demands on the same resource. The interaction belongs to the relation among the controls and shared resource, not necessarily to either control's implementation.
topology: Two independently valid controls converge on their shared resource; conflict is relational.
required_terms: Incompatible demands\ conflict lives in the relation, not either control
bw_encoding: White ordinary nodes and groups; labels and boundaries carry roles without decorative tones.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames. Grayscale refinement: Paired controls distinguished from shared resource and dashed conflict region. Fidelity pass: Restored check marks on both individually correct controls; conflict remains on their shared relation.
alt: Two control nodes — Control A, which requires a squashed commit, and Control B, which rejects a broad diff — each correct when read alone. Both point by a solid arrow to one explicit shared resource, the commit set, that they act on. Below the commit set, a dashed-outline box marks the incompatible demands: the conflict belongs to the relation among the two controls and the resource they share, not to either control's own implementation. A check mark on each control indicates that each is individually correct.
